_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-15. Sources: boston/FLEET-ECONOMICS-BOSTON.md + boston/TRACKER-SNAPSHOT-2026-08-15.md. Per module: 'copy' renders VERBATIM; 'data' is structured values Grok formats. Underscore-prefixed fields are non-renderable guard notes — never reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing (fail closed). This is fleet financing only — the equity/fundraise/defense/Gulf content firewalls in FLEET-INVESTORS-BRIEF.md §5 apply in full. Every economic figure renders WITH its assumption label; ranges only, no point estimates. D6 LOCKED: anchor-plus-fill leads; seat-band fill is upside, never headline.

copy.headline: Own the fleet behind Boston's water commuter network.
copy.subline: Anchor revenue is contracted before capital deploys. Seat-band fill is upside on top — never the base case.

roles: Fleet Investor — owns/finances the Boston fleet (workboat-grade N45s; N30 where corridor-appropriate).
Operator — runs the service (crewing, operations); existing Boston operators are natural candidates. No operator is committed.
Navier — supplies vessels, software, and the network platform.

Employers — contract committed seat bundles at market per-seat prices — the schedule spine and largest single revenue layer. Employer block commitments accelerate the launch trigger; no scenario depends on an above-market anchor subsidy.
Public Partners — grant landings at existing piers and marina berths; no terminal construction.
copy.trigger: Corridors launch only at 60–80 committed seats. Capital deploys behind committed demand, not ahead of it.

copy.redeployability: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market: the 7-city network is the residual-value story.

data.inherit: unchanged (Decision D3 — same corridor map as the employer site)

copy.trigger_explainer: Each corridor activates only when 60–80 seats are committed. Launch timing honesty: end-2027 earliest.

demand_pool.standing_label: Indicative of demand potential along these corridors — not commitments or commercial relationships.

data.capture_assumption: 3.0% of on-site headcount (tracker's own stated input)
honesty_notes: 5 of 10 tracked nodes have zero sourced headcount — pools understate.
BOS-5 carries the largest sourced pool (North Station + Encore) but is a phase-3 line with zero launch-phase vessels — that demand is not actionable at launch under current phasing.

copy.rules: Named employers appear only as indicative demand potential under the standing label — never as customers, partners, or LOI signatories. Blank tracker cells stay blank.

pnl.structure: utilization_stack (D6′ LOCKED 2026-08-15, supersedes anchor-first): committed bundles → spot seats → experiences & charters → upside lines (sponsorship, overnight cargo) → opex → network share → scenario payback

lines.label: Canon 4.1 kWh/nm @ $0.30/kWh × stacked daily activity (commute legs + midday/evening/weekend sailings). Electric-operation assumption.
N45 NOT validated — N30 canon ($65K/yr) floor, $100K/yr stated ceiling assumption, ÷12.

Benchmark-validated 2026-08-15 — 2-crew (captain + deckhand), $85/hr combined loaded, extended to stacked hours. Basis: BLS OEWS Boston metro means (May 2023) x 1.4294 ECEC burden = $77.16/hr; $85 = ~3%/yr wage drift to 2026 (assumption, labeled). Shift structure (split shifts for 16-hr stacked day) to ops walkthrough. Source: handoff/archetypes/CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS.md
Placeholder, weak basis — hull/liability ~1.5–3%/yr of insured value + illustrative berth fee loosely anchored to one documented commercial rate; not a Navier-specific quote.

network_share.value: 10% of gross revenue, off the top
network_share.label: canon

payback_summary.label: Indicative ranges only, conservative default. Upside comes from utilization layers with cited market prices and from more corridors activating — never from inflating per-layer assumptions.

speed_relief_upside_row.label: With authority speed-rule relief (precedent: Stockholm Candela P-12 exemption)
speed_relief_upside_row.note: Not quantified for Boston this pass — renders as a labeled upside row without numbers. Never blended into base or mid cases; base economics respect posted limits.

stack_layers.frame: One asset, one day, four demand layers. A commuter-only vessel monetizes ~15% of available hours; the stack monetizes the day. Commute is the strategic backbone and schedule spine; experiences, charters, spot and overnight lines buy down payback. Sources: REVENUE-LEVER-BENCHMARKS.md + CARGO-LAYER-BENCHMARKS.md (operator, year, URL, confidence per rate).

layers.name: Committed commuter bundles
layers.pricing: $950–1,275/seat-month — priced as a discounted pass vs premium spot (industry pass discounts 26–51%: MBTA ~26%, Seastreak 40-trip ~35%, NYC Ferry ~36%, Blade ~44–51%); 3–4× MBTA monthly ($319); ~50–60% below door-to-door substitute (Uber Salem→Boston ~$56/trip ≈ $2,460/mo)
layers.status: Benchmark-anchored; canon-consistent; no Boston operations yet

layers.name: Spot seats (residual commute capacity + shoulder sailings)
layers.pricing: $40–65/leg, yield-managed — bounded by Seastreak $30 and Uber door-to-door ~$55–56; matches approved corridor fare (Boston↔Hingham $65)
layers.status: Benchmark-anchored; fill rates unproven, modeled thin (10–30%)

layers.name: Experiences & private charters (midday/evening/weekend)
layers.pricing: Experiences $59–79/pp (Boston market: BHCC sunset $49 → Odyssey dinner $77–98, whale watch $75); charters $550–600/hr (Boston Charter Boat $550/hr, 25-pax, 2-hr min)
layers.status: Market-priced (Boston operators cited); not yet operated by Navier; conservative case ≈ ⅓ of one incumbent daily sailing

layers.name: Sponsorship (upside only)
layers.pricing: $150K/yr fleet-level placeholder — precedents: Citi Bike ~$7–8M/yr system, Santander Cycles £6.25M/yr, Cleveland HealthLine line-naming $250K/yr, Barclays station $200K/yr
layers.status: Precedent-priced; no marine-transit precedent; never per-vessel headline

layers.name: Overnight cargo runs (upside only)
layers.pricing: ~$350/run contract, 16 nights/mo — anchored to published waterborne tariffs (Casco Bay Lines 2026: $0.108–0.162/kg generic freight ⇒ $216–324 per ~2,000 kg run) + medical-courier premiums (Dropoff 2026: $30–100/job, refrigerated $3.50–5.25/mi)
layers.status: Published-tariff-anchored; not yet operated by Navier; harbor cargo earns courier-linehaul rates, NOT island air-substitute rates ($0.75–1.50/kg canon does not apply where roads exist). First cargo classes: medical/lab specimens, batch parcels, catering/event — clean, high-value, night-moving. Seafood REJECTED as first class (odor/leakage/sanitation in premium cabin; commodity-priced $2.50–3.75/box)

scenarios.label: Per-vessel N45 ($2.5M capex), no anchor subsidy in any case. Ranges + assumptions, conservative default. Every unproven layer enters base case only at deliberately thin utilization.

table.payback: ~21 yr — cash-positive but not financeable; deliberately punitive fills

table.note: Includes sponsorship ($3.1K/mo per vessel, fleet-level ÷4) + overnight cargo ($5.6K/mo). Converges with canon partner-corridor payback (Boston↔Hingham 2.49 yr) — same physics: all-day premium utilization.

scenarios.honesty_note: Mid case is the financeable headline — requires L3 execution at roughly half the sailing cadence of Boston's incumbent experience operators, at prices below their dinner tier. Conservative shown always. Upside labeled. Crew rate benchmark-validated vs BLS Boston (loaded mean $77.16/hr May 2023; model uses $85 with wage-drift buffer); shift structure pending ops walkthrough.

launch.label: Minimum viable launch fleet — 1–2 vessels per phase-1 line, sized to trigger-scale AM/PM peak sailings, not continuous headway. Derived, not published. No spares margin included.

full_build.label: 60-minute continuous-headway ceiling — an illustrative capacity-ceiling planning tool, not a timetable or day-1 requirement. Dwell/turnaround/headway are illustrative assumptions.

data.spares_note: No maintenance-reserve/spare vessel included in any count; a real fleet plan typically adds ~10–15% spares capacity (not computed this pass).

cards.title: Demand-gated launch
cards.body: Corridors launch only at 60–80 committed seats — capital deploys behind committed demand, not ahead of it.

cards.title: Redeployable network asset
cards.body: Workboat-grade N45s redeploy across the 7-city network; a vessel is not stranded in one market.

cards.title: Navier platform continuity
cards.body: Vessels, software, demand generation, and the network platform stay with Navier across operators and cities.

cards.title: Phased fleet growth
cards.body: Fleet scales with corridor activation — launch fleet first, growth tranches only as corridors hit trigger.
